newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - June US T-bonds seen building for swing.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - June US T-bonds seen building for swing.

text.p: The narrow range that has confined June U.S. Treasury bond futures in the last few days could persist near-term and help lay a base for a substantial price swing in the next few weeks, technicians said.

After the roughly 10-point breakdown since early December, the June T-bond is "catching its breath" and could continue to waffle between about the mid-106 and high-108 areas for the next two weeks, said Robert Zukowski, senior capital markets technician, Pegasus Econometric Group.
"It seems like bonds are waiting for the next cue or the next shoe to drop," he said.

Zukowski said June bonds had been sorely oversold and showed signs suggesting a short-term bottom might have been formed in the 106-00 to 107-00 area. But the bounce back up thus far has proved limited and failed to confirm a bottom.
"I am looking for the market to remain very rangebound," Terence Gabriel, technical analyst, IDEA Inc, told Reuters Financial Television of his outlook for the next few days.
But he said the contract was building pressure for "quite a substantial resolution" of three or four full points either up or down, a move that could occur in the next week.
"I do think next week will be quite a wild ride," he said.
Bruce Kamich, senior vice president, MCM MoneyWatch, called nearby T-bonds "pretty boring on a short-term basis."
But he said June T-bonds could be close to setting a seven-week cycle low near 107-00, possibly next week.
"Then we can line up a better rally into May, despite FOMC," he said, adding that the contract could rise by two or three points to as high as 110-00 into the May 20 FOMC meeting.
"I think that's (rally) going to take us into May, but it may fall short of it (110)," Kamich added.
Until next week's swing, Gabriel expected that any rise into the 108-08/32 to 16/32 region would promote selling.
A pullback toward 106-29/32 support, however, could draw enough buying to fuel a return into the mid-107 level, Gabriel noted.

A strong close above 108-07/32 "might be the trigger that compels shortcovering and fresh new buying," Zukowski said, adding that a rise above the 109-00 level was more likely to entice new buyers to enter. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
